script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: small-town life

Begin screenplay.

Title: The Last Tree

INT. MAIN STREET - DAY

The sun bathes the small, quiet town of Eldridge in a warm light. People walk around, greeting each other with friendly smiles. This is the kind of place where everyone knows everyone, and everyone looks out for one another.

JANE (40s, determined and caring) enters the scene, her eyes scanning the familiar faces. She looks worn out, carrying a heavy burden. A local, JANE has dedicated her life to the community and its people.

Suddenly, JANE spots a man, MARK (30s, mysterious and troubled), sitting alone on a bench, staring into the distance. He seems out of place, a stranger in this idyllic town.

INT. JANE'S HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Jane sits at her kitchen table, her face etched with concern. She speaks into the phone.

JANE
(into phone)
Yes, Officer, I saw him. The newcomer. He was on Main Street, sitting on that bench. He looked sad, almost defeated. I've never seen him around here before.

INT. MARK'S RV - LIVING ROOM - DAY

Mark sits alone in his RV, surrounded by an eclectic collection of items. He seems lost in thought as he looks at an old photograph of a smiling family.

MARK (voiced over)
I used to belong somewhere. But now, all I have is this old RV and the open road.

EXT. ELDRIDGE PARK - DAY

Jane walks through the park, her thoughts consumed by Mark. She finds him sitting on a bench, staring at the last remaining tree in the town.

JANE
Hello, Mark. What brings you to Eldridge?

MARK
Just passing through, I guess. But something about this place... it feels different.

JANE
This town has a way of making you feel at home, even when you're lost.

INT. JANE'S KITCHEN - NIGHT

Jane cooks dinner for Mark, who seems hesitant at first but eventually sits down to eat with her.

JANE
You know, Eldridge used to be known for its beautiful forest. But a disease killed all the trees, save for this last one. It's a symbol of resilience, of hope in the face of adversity.

MARK
(pausing)
I lost my family in a fire. I've been on the road ever since, trying to outrun the memories.

JANE
(gently)
You don't have to run, Mark. You can start rebuilding your life here in Eldridge.

INT. ELDRIDGE PARK - DAY

Jane and Mark stand in front of the last tree, their hands intertwined. They look up at the tree, its leaves rustling gently in the breeze.

JANE
(whispering)
Let's plant something new. Something that can grow and thrive, just like this tree.

Mark nods in agreement as they turn to leave the park, their hearts filled with the promise of a new beginning.

FADE OUT.

THE END
